court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Nagpur, Hindu Marriage Petition No.34 of 2007
case_name: Shri Sunil S/O Ganesh Hiranwar vs Smt. Beena W/O Sunil Hiranwar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Shri Sunil s/o Ganesh Hiranwar, husband
parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Beena w/o Sunil Hiranwar, wife

facts_of_case: The parties got married in 1999 and had a son born in 2000. The husband filed for divorce under Section 13(1) (i-a) and (i-b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, while the wife sought restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Act. The trial court dismissed the petition for divorce and allowed the petition for restitution.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove specific instances of such conduct.
legal_principles.held: Though the husband has not specifically pleaded the particulars in respect of the acts of cruelty by the wife, on an overall reading of the pleadings and the evidence, it is clear that the wife had treated the husband with cruelty.
cited_cases: AIR 2002 SC 88 (Adhyatma Bhattar Alwar v. Adhyatma Bhattar Sri Devi)

legal_principles.principle: A marriage is considered dead for all practical purposes if there is no chance of retrieval.
legal_principles.held: The marriage is dead for all practical purposes and the continuation of such a marriage, of which there is no chance of retrieval, would itself amount to cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The final order granted a decree of divorce to the husband.
